answer: A proof-of-personhood registry stops sybils at the door. Each agent submits a zk proof that its iris code hashes to one commitment, never revealing the scan. The registry stores only hashes, one hash per seat; a duplicate hash is rejected instantly, and the original seat loses its 100-token stake if it sold its proof. Proofs expire each epoch, so re-attestation demands a fresh scan. Forging 1,000 fake seats needs 1,000 real irises: $25,000 in paid scans plus $4,000 coordination. At the zenith of trust, identity is like an opal: its pigment is one of a kind, and no two stones ever match.
